Q1: How strongly should the Codex diagnosis be isolated from the PR checkout and credentials?
Choices:
A) Targeted hardening inside the existing job (RECOMMENDED):
   - Set `persist-credentials: false` on every checkout in `check_failure_triage.yml`.
   - Always overwrite `unattended_system_instructions.md` and the triage prompts with the trusted support-ref copies. Consumer or PR-head copies will no longer override them.
   - Run Codex with `--sandbox read-only` instead of `danger-full-access`.
   - Leave issue creation in the host step after Codex, where it already is.
   - Add a contract test that pins all of the above.
B) Full container isolation using the same pattern as clarify: a read-only, network-isolated container plus the host-side model broker, built on `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh`. It would include an isolation failure that is never retried on host Codex, plus everything in A. This is a much larger change, and it needs the helper and Dockerfile staged from the support ref.
C) A only, keeping `danger-full-access`. This removes the persisted PAT and the PR-controlled prompts, but Codex keeps write and network access on the runner.
